# Launch Your Own AI Web App with Hugging Face Spaces

> **In short:** A Hugging Face Space is a small web app that runs an AI demo. You can make your own copy of someone else's Space with **Duplicate this Space**. Hugging Face's docs say most app Spaces need a paid plan, but free personal accounts in good standing can host up to 2 Gradio Spaces that run on ZeroGPU.

Want your own AI demo with a link you can share? Instead of building one from scratch, you can copy a ready-made Space into your account and run it there. This guide follows Hugging Face's official documentation and tells you up front what is free and what isn't.

## Before you start

- **A Hugging Face account.** Sign up at [huggingface.co](https://huggingface.co) if you don't have one.
- **Know the free option.** According to Hugging Face's docs, Static Spaces are free for everyone, while Gradio and Docker Spaces need a paid plan to create or duplicate. The exception: a free personal account in good standing (verified email, account older than 30 days) can host up to 2 ZeroGPU Spaces. ZeroGPU works only with Gradio Spaces.
- **A short name for your app,** in lowercase with hyphens, such as `my-first-demo`. It becomes part of the app's address.
- **About 10 minutes.**

## Step 1: Find a demo to copy

Go to [huggingface.co/spaces](https://huggingface.co/spaces) and browse or search for a demo you like. If you want to stay on the free option, pick a Gradio Space that runs on ZeroGPU. Hugging Face's ZeroGPU docs link to a [curated list of ZeroGPU Spaces](https://huggingface.co/spaces/enzostvs/zero-gpu-spaces). Open the Space and try it once to make sure it works.

You'll know it worked when the demo loads on its page and responds to your input.

## Step 2: Duplicate the Space

Hugging Face's docs say: click the **three dots** at the top right of the Space and click **Duplicate this Space**. A form opens where you set up your copy.

You'll know it worked when you see the duplication form with fields such as the owner and the Space name.

## Step 3: Fill in the form

The docs list what you can change:

- **Owner:** your account (or an organization where you can write).
- **Space name:** the short name you picked.
- **Visibility:** a duplicated Space is **private by default**. Choose **public** if you want others to open it.
- **Hardware:** for the free option, choose **ZeroGPU** if your account qualifies. Hugging Face says duplicated Spaces use CPU Basic by default, and duplicating a Gradio or Docker Space otherwise needs a paid plan.
- **Secrets and variables:** if the original Space uses them, the form shows them. Public variables are filled in for you; secrets (such as API keys) you must add yourself, and Hugging Face warns you about them.

Then confirm the duplication.

You'll know it worked when you are taken to your new Space's page under your own account.

## Step 4: Wait for it to build

Your copy now builds and starts. This can take a few minutes, depending on the app. When it's ready, the demo appears on the page just like the original. On free hardware, Hugging Face says a Space goes to sleep after a period without use, and the next visitor wakes it up again.

You'll know it worked when your copy of the demo loads and responds the same way the original did.

## Step 5: Test it and share the link

Try the demo with your own input. To share it, copy the address of your Space page, which looks like `huggingface.co/spaces/[your-username]/[your-space-name]`. A public Space can also be opened through its own web address ending in `.hf.space`. On ZeroGPU Spaces, each visitor has a daily GPU quota: Hugging Face lists 2 minutes for visitors who aren't signed in and 5 minutes for free accounts.

💬 Example: "I made my own copy of an AI demo. Try it here: [link to your Space]"

You'll know it worked when someone else can open your link and use the demo.

## Common mistakes

- **Leaving the Space private.** Duplicates are private by default, and other people get an error page. *The fix:* Set visibility to **public** in the form, or later in your Space's **Settings**.
- **Expecting every Space to be free to copy.** Gradio and Docker Spaces need a paid plan, except the ZeroGPU option for qualifying free personal accounts. *The fix:* Pick a ZeroGPU Space and select ZeroGPU hardware.
- **Missing secrets.** Some Spaces need an API key to work. *The fix:* Read the warning in the form and add your own secret, or choose a Space that doesn't need one.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** You can keep a favorite AI demo in your own account and share it with friends and family.
- **For your business or work:** You can show colleagues a working AI demo in minutes, before anyone invests in building a real tool. Don't put private or customer data into a public Space.
- **If you're just getting started:** Duplicate one small ZeroGPU demo, make it public, and open the link on another device to see that it works.

## Try it now

Open the [curated list of ZeroGPU Spaces](https://huggingface.co/spaces/enzostvs/zero-gpu-spaces), pick one demo, and click the three dots › **Duplicate this Space**. Set it to public, choose ZeroGPU hardware, and send yourself the link.
